script: "I sued for $100,000 after a taco ruined me—judge blew my case!". 2024. I landed in New York City, all bright lights and big dreams, thinking I'd soak up the American hustle. First stop: Los Tacos No 1 in Times Square. I was like, "No questions, no clarifications—just give me the salsa." I am a heat‑wimp, certified by my own kitchen experiments, so I know spicy is a no‑no. But the taco crew handed me a salsa jar like it was a freebie. I took a bite, my mouth turned to fire, and I knew I was in trouble. So I filed a pro‑se suit for $100,000, claiming the staff didn't warn me about the heat. The judge, with a smirk, said, "You knew it was spicy. If you're going to grab a salsa, you better ask." He even quipped, "When it comes to salsa, the spice is often the point." (I know, right?) Next, I hit a Walmart in New Jersey, desperate for Wi‑Fi to post my travel vlog. Their login screen demanded a U.S. phone number—no German number, no luck. I couldn't connect, my heart sank, and I sued for $10 million, accusing the store of emotional distress and discrimination against international numbers. The judge laughed, "Title VI and civil rights don't protect phone numbers that aren't U.S." (Literally insane.) The last act: back in Times Square, I saw two men harrying a homeless guy. I called the police, but by the time they arrived the thugs were gone, and the officers flat‑out refused to take a statement. I felt flashbacks, PTSD, insomnia—so I filed another $10 million claim. The city's legal team slammed my complaint, and after a quick review I dropped the suit and went back to my part‑time law studies in Germany. (Honestly, I am still better than them.)
